production_factory_gate.finding: bootstrap_narrowing_manager_in_transaction builds the base BootstrapNarrowingManager whose open_pair, start_and_wait, unmask and is_ready refuse unconditionally; no runtime input makes them succeed. The implemented delegations exist only on the private _PrototypeBootstrapManager, which nothing outside tests selects.
production_factory_gate.decision: Refusal maintained. Required inputs and native evidence are not all present, so no factory change was made or proposed for merge.
production_factory_gate.legitimate_path: After C2, F1-F4 and native qualification, a reviewed code change selects the already implemented delegation (open_pair -> _publish_and_inspect_pair, start_and_wait -> _start_bound_audit/_start_bound_commission, is_ready -> retained-publication-bracketed _bound_helper_ready).

missing_software_wiring_ranked: Protected interactive publishers for admission.json, installed-files.json, loaded-units.json and policy.json (the next step after validation/preview in the selected sequence, docs/runtime-activation-remaining.md:1962-1964). A bootstrap-layout check on installed-files candidates would require refactoring the admission measurement and was not done; admission still enforces it.
owner_supplied_inputs_procedure: 1. Generate an Ed25519 keypair on an owner-controlled device; the private key never enters the repo, logs, Issues or the VM.
2. Compute the fingerprint sha256:<SHA-256 of the raw 32-byte public key> and convey it out of band.
3. On the VM as root on a tty: python -m azazel_nexus.operator_enrollment enroll <label> (paste key, fingerprint, type ENROLL <label>).
4. Place canonical root-owned /etc/azazel/bootstrap/policy.json (operators, max_seconds chosen by owner).

6. Review and place admission.json (package digest from az-nexus-bootstrap observe-packages, installed-files manifest digest, systemd profile digest, floors/limits, audit head) and installed-files.json.

7. Publish deployment.json (6 fields; digests derived, epoch/revocation/operator chosen by owner): azazel-nexus bootstrap-deployment-preview < file, then azazel-nexus bootstrap-deployment-initialize on a root tty.
8. Publish the bootstrap generation (az-nexus-bootstrap generation-preview / generation-publish).

9. Per boot: publish selection.json for the current boot_id with a fresh approval_id (azazel-nexus bootstrap-selection-initialize); mint the time anchor (az-nexus-bootstrap time-initialize); sign approval.json off-host and place approval.json + 64-byte approval.sig.
corrections: The same trace reported no installed-files manifest generator; `azazel-nexus installed-files-candidate` already provides a context-free canonical candidate (src/azazel_nexus/installed_candidate.py:146-165, cli.py:743-756).

An initial provisioning trace reported the deployment and selection publishers as unexposed; an independent check found them exposed as azazel-nexus bootstrap-deployment-{preview,initialize,recover} and bootstrap-selection-{initialize,recover} (src/azazel_nexus/cli.py:734-740, 804-807, 910-930; pyproject.toml:31). No CLI change is needed.

known_limitations: Until cross-boot renewal exists a node bootstraps once; retry needs clean state (VM snapshot revert), never deletion of retained records
Prestart and generation admission run before the kernel guard is armed; bounded by the controller unit TimeoutStartSec=30s with TimeoutStartFailureMode=kill (pre-READY)
Genesis single use is enforced only by the non-empty-ledger refusal; a wiped ledger plus a fresh signed approval would be accepted again; assurance LOCAL_CONTINUITY_ONLY
